document.title: [Excised]/Pakistan Interservice Intelligence/Pakistan Directorate Supplying the Taliban Forces
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Secret] The ISI is supplying the Taliban with munitions, fuel and food, using a private sector transportation company to funnel supplies into Afghanistan. Food convoys are open, but munitions convoys depart late in the evening and are concealed.

events.description: The report states that ISI is currently using a private-sector transportation company to funnel supplies (munitions, fuel, lubricants, food) to Taliban forces in Afghanistan via vehicle convoys on three routes.
Omar was reported to be in Kandahar and to intend to relocate to Kabul once the situation there settled, while still controlling the Taliban situation from outside Kabul.

ISI is reported to be using a private transportation company running vehicle convoys to supply Taliban forces with munitions, fuel, oil, lubricants and food via three routes. Munitions convoys depart late evening and are concealed.
Intelligence Information Report to DIA Washington on ISI supply of Taliban forces.
Omar is in Kandahar, controlling the Taliban situation from outside Kabul and intending to relocate to Kabul once things settle.

key_claims: ISI was using a private-sector transportation company to supply the Taliban with munitions, fuel, lubricants and food in October 1996.
Munitions convoys depart Pakistan late in the evening, and all convoys are concealed to hide their contents.
Three supply routes were used: Peshawar-Jalalabad-Kabul (the most frequently used), Quetta-Kandahar-Kabul, and Miran Shah-Khost-Kabul.
The Taliban leader (Omar) was in Kandahar and planned to move to Kabul once the situation there settled.
Omar was still controlling the Taliban situation from outside Kabul.
